label: canon-b18-gm-n2
_why: BATCH 2 OF THE FOUR-BATCH PLAN PROPOSED 2026-09-16 (HANDOVER.md; awaiting the user's go-ahead - NOT to be launched without it): THE INPUT-VALUE STEP, GAIN-MATCHED - the design's own price channel, and the raw sector's weight. FINDINGS F127 read the found configuration's old rung against vanilla measured the same way: rung-0 workers 3.4-3.8M world-wide against vanilla's 7.3-9.5M on the same methods (0.35-0.45M in the majors against 1.1-2.5M), value added per worker 1-5% of the industry's frontier in every industry - the old rung is out-competed twenty to a hundred times over and stays 45% staffed only because nobody hires its people: the tiered sector employs 36-40M where vanilla's employs 71-73M in the same buildings (2.5x the value added on half the levels, 72-74% of all building VA against vanilla's 31-35%), and the raw sector beside it is 59-63% of vanilla's extraction levels and 69-74% of its agricultural VA, because the frontier's input ladder (B 1.5 per era) grows far slower than its output ladder (A 2.2). Every willingness lever is closed (F100 / F120 / F126), the lift is closed (F118 / F119) and the eager defines are closed (F125); what remains is labour absorption - more buildings per unit of GDP - on the two axes the sweep never moved. THIS BOOK MOVES B: the frontier's input value x 1.8^era in place of x 1.5^era over each rung's own vanilla mix (textile e2: 103.7 fabric + 17.3 dye + 8.6 tools for the same 217.8 clothes, against 72 + 12 + 6; steel e3: 301.7 iron + 90.5 coal + 90.5 electricity against 174.6 + 52.4 + 52.4), rung 0 untouched. That is the mechanism CLAUDE.md names for obsolescence - the old rung dies when its input prices rise while its output price falls - applied through the frontier's own demand, and it lowers value added per frontier level to 0.77-0.80x the found book's, i.e. more levels and more workers per unit of GDP. ⭐ GAIN-MATCHED PER ERA: the cost ladder is set so the frontier's value added per construction point equals the found book's at e1, e2 and e3 (make_ab_config --cost-ladder 1.52,2.79,5.34: 600 / 912 / 1,674 / 3,204 in the 600-class, 800 / 1,216 / 2,232 / 4,272 in the 800-class), because the sweep showed the loop gain is the steepest lever there is (C 1.6 -> 1.98x, 1.9 -> 1.08x, 2.05 -> 0.72x) and an unmatched B would confound the axis with it. A-down (the frontier's productivity per worker) is the other axis; it runs against the workers-per-capita band the user centred on the design's own goal (0.634x), so B goes first.

_delta: Against canon-c19-in12 (the found configuration): B 1.8 in place of 1.5 (input value on every rung above era 0) and the per-era cost ladder that holds the frontier's value added per construction point at the found book's; A 2.2, the x1.2 lift on rung 0, ai_value 3^era, the divisor, the defines, the research events and the 24-month bar identical.

_predictions._structure: Pre-registered before launch, per the no-extrapolation rule. Two KEY predictions, one on the raw sector (the mechanism), one on the old rung (the goal); the endpoint on alignment_check.mjs. The gain match is at BASE prices - a raw sector pulled to higher prices lowers the frontier's realised margin by an amount nothing here predicts, which is the WATCH item.
_predictions.KEY_1_the_raw_pull: THE MECHANISM: extraction levels (mines, logging, oil, rubber, fishing, whaling) at 1935 at or above 11,000 world-wide (found 9,221 / 9,356; vanilla 15,613 / 14,937), and the raw inputs in the British market at 1935 above the found book's readings - fabric at or above 108% of base (found 102 / 95), iron at or above 118% (113 / 113), coal at or above 110% (109 / 97). NULL: extraction under 10,000 AND raw prices within 5 points of the found book's.
_predictions.KEY_2_the_old_rung: THE GOAL: rung 0's world workers at or below 2.8M (found 3.40M / 3.28M), its staffing at or below 40% (found 45%), and the textile rung-0 value added per staffed level at or below 400 pounds a week (found 544) - squeezed from both ends (dearer fabric, cheaper clothes). NULL: staffing at or above 43% with workers above 3.1M.
_predictions.endpoint: world GDP 0.95-1.20x vanilla at 1935 (gain-matched, so the found book's level or a little above it as cheaper absolute rungs fill earlier); productive workers per capita 0.68-0.80x - the top of the band or just above it, which is the point: more levels and more raw jobs per unit of GDP. THE RUN-LEVEL STOP APPLIES (a run above 1.3x at 1936 ends the configuration).
_predictions.prices: the tiered goods at 1935 (British market) at or below the found book's: clothes at or below 85% of base (found 87 / 97), tools at or below 75% (81 / 70), steel at or below 70% (73 / 73) - the same output on richer inputs is more output value per level, i.e. more supply.
_predictions.labour: world strict unemployment 20-27% (found 30.5 / 26.6%), shortlist peasant-inclusive 32-40% (found 41.2 / 39.9%); tiered levels at 1935 12,000-15,000 (found 9,917-10,633).
_predictions.hoard_and_dip: pools 0.35-0.65 of world GDP; the 1900 dip UNCHANGED at 0.75-0.90 (e1's cost is matched too, so the early game is the found book's); the capital-abundance flag as the found book's.
_predictions.WATCH_the_realised_margin: the frontier's margin at 1935 (e2 / e3, profit / (VA - profit)) against the found book's 44-54%: under 30% with GDP under 0.9x means the base-price gain match overstated the realised gain (the raw pull ate it) - the branch is the ladder 10% cheaper (--cost-ladder 1.37,2.51,4.81), not a new axis.
_predictions.perf: row P total within +10% of the vanilla median; richer recipes add goods flows, not buildings - no reason to expect a cost.

_alignment: THE 2+1 RULE (user-ruled 2026-09-14, F114): after run 2, `node tools/testbed/ledger/alignment_check.mjs --arm <session>:canon-b18-gm` - world GDP and productive workers per capita at 1935 against the vanilla per-run median, five bands each; a pair fails an axis only in different bands AND >= 0.15 (GDP) / >= 0.10 (workers) apart. DIVERGENT => canon_b18_gm_tb.json as its own session, the reading the median of three. PLUS THE RUN-LEVEL STOP and THE CAPITAL-ABUNDANCE FLAG (`capital_flags.mjs`, shortlist-wide = VOID, exit 4).
_comparison: vanilla n=18 for every ratio; canon-c19-in12 is the one-lever baseline (F117 sessions 20260914_173832 + 20260914_204329): GDP 1.09 / 1.07x, workers 0.65 / 0.67x, rung 0 45% at 3.40 / 3.28M workers, extraction levels 9,221 / 9,356, tiered levels 10,633 / 9,917, hoard 0.64 / 0.42, strict unemployment 30.5 / 26.6% world. F127 holds the per-industry and sector tables.
_branches: Above 1.3x at 1936 -> the config ends; next = the ladder 10% dearer (--cost-ladder 1.67,3.07,5.87). Below 0.8x in both seeds -> the ladder 10% cheaper (--cost-ladder 1.37,2.51,4.81). In band with KEY 1 met -> batch 3 = the second step, B 2.0 gain-matched (--cost-ladder 1.27,2.15,4.00), or the e2soft combination if batch 1 filled the dip; KEY 1 null -> the B axis closes, batch 3 = A-down gain-matched (A 1.9, --cost-ladder 1.38,2.22,3.68) pending the user's ruling on the workers band.
_watch: every run ~5 min in: tools/testbed/batch_heartbeat.sh <session> - the mod marker, the version, this run's error window BY POSITION, the clock, CRASHED lines, DEFINE REJECTED (the canon's defines only; no rejection line expected)
first run: first_run_decomp.mjs, capital_flags.mjs, queue_series.mjs, rung0_path.mjs, the F127 sector split (extraction / agriculture levels and VA) and the British raw prices from markets.tsv
post-run: alignment_check.mjs, capital_flags.mjs, company_check.mjs, preflight -Session, VERDICT.md, SESSION_VERDICTS row, FINDINGS, the ledger
_cost: 2 x 1836->1936 ~ 2 x 2h35 ~ 5 h, plus a third run on divergence.
_caveats: n=2 by design; the alignment tool decides on the third.

Launch ONLY through tools/testbed/launch_detached.ps1 CALLED DIRECTLY from the PowerShell tool (landmine L30); the STOP file must be absent; the five-minute smoke check on EVERY run; never interleave configs (one schedule = one config).

Two things change in the config (B and the cost ladder) under ONE design rule (gain matching at base prices); the rule is stated so a result can be attributed to the axis and not to the loop gain, and the WATCH item is where that attribution can fail.

The absolute rungs are cheaper than the found book's (e3 3,204 / 4,272 against 4,115 / 5,487); the pool's cost divisor is pinned at 0.000125 like every sweep book, so the private pool divides the top rung by 1.53 instead of 1.69 - a small, stated difference.
